front: How do you compare two models on cost?

back: Predict its effect on cost per call and on cost per completed task. A cache hit lowers the first; only a steady success rate carries it to the second.
front: What do you do before you measure a cut in cost?

back: A check that stops a run when its token or cost budget is spent, and keeps the trace of what it did.
The wait from sending a request to the first token of the reply. It is one part of latency, next to the time to generate the reply and the time tools take.
front: What is time to first token?

back: A limit on how long a task may take from start to end, set before you measure the work.
Its runs cost less each, but fewer of them complete. The cost of the runs that fail is still paid, so it is spread over fewer successes.
